hints: The ordered distances for the 11 Lakeview pupils are: 10, 14, 19, 22, 26, 27, 28, 30, 32, 33, 41.
With $n = 11$, the lower quartile $Q_1$ is the 3rd value and the upper quartile $Q_3$ is the 9th value.
Subtract $Q_1$ from $Q_3$ to find the interquartile range: $\operatorname{IQR} = 32 - 19$.
walkthrough:
List the ordered distances for Lakeview school ($n = 11$):
$$10, \; 14, \; \textbf{19}, \; 22, \; 26, \; 27, \; 28, \; 30, \; \textbf{32}, \; 33, \; 41$$

Identify the quartiles:
$$Q_1 = 19\text{ m} \quad (\text{3rd value})$$
$$Q_3 = 32\text{ m} \quad (\text{9th value})$$

Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 32 - 19 = 13\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Determine the positions of the quartiles for $n = 11$.
- The median is the 6th value ($27$ m).
- The lower half of the data consists of the 5 values below the median: $10, 14, 19, 22, 26$.
  The lower quartile $Q_1$ is the middle of these 5 values, which is the 3rd overall value:
  $$Q_1 = 19\text{ m}$$
- The upper half consists of the 5 values above the median: $28, 30, 32, 33, 41$.
  The upper quartile $Q_3$ is the middle of these 5 values, which is the 9th overall value:
  $$Q_3 = 32\text{ m}$$

Step 2: Compute the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 32 - 19 = 13\text{ m}$$
